question: Which persistent anchor and transient annotation contracts can share native mapping without merging their lifetimes?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest pursue verdict, at queue position 20. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: One document model; selection, focus, projection, annotation index and paint stay per mounted view.
Application metadata, persistent target, exact-view index and decoration paint keep separate lifetimes and owners.
The public borrowed target is scalar and resolve-only; batching or collection mapping stays private unless a measured job proves otherwise.
Deletion policies are truthful. nearest owns durable fallback and history recovery, and drop owns locally observed terminal invalidation, not a convergent CRDT promise.
Explicit owner cleanup, deterministic overlap, duplicate-ID failure and omitted-DOM remount hold; no kernel replacement without a matched scale win.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 09-20 consumer census, the 09-21 final-pass and OSS comparison across nine editor families, the adoption execution's verified Chromium and package receipts and its matched view-index benchmark, and the 09-30 content-root executions. Rechecked on the live tree the plitejs/annotations exports and store contract, the React hook, the Comments per-view index and nearest deletion, anchor drop handling, the comment-mode example, and the root and Plite vision text. No tests, browser or benchmark were run.
summary: The job is to keep application metadata, persistent anchor identity, a per-view resolved index and inline paint as separate lifetimes over one document, so accepted and proposed views can resolve the same target differently. Live plitejs/annotations exposes only createAnnotationStore and its typed reader (resolve-only AnnotationAnchor, per-node and per-id reads, change routing by node key). React gets useAnnotationStore per mounted view, Comments keeps one index per view and uses deletion: 'nearest', and drop stays terminal local invalidation. The 09-21 adoption removed the generic provider and public diagnostics, moved comment mode to two mounted views over one model, and kept the node-key mapping kernel after native batching, a collection-mapped prototype and simpler snapshots all failed the frozen promotion gate. The strongest alternatives each lose a hard job (inline everything into Comments, CodeMirror or Monaco-style flat range sets, attachment IDs as document marks, one store shared across views). They lose neutral reuse across Plite and Plate, tree and root identity, the external thread lifecycle, or per-view projection. One teaching defect remains outside the architecture. Root VISION.md still says annotations use their own provider and names <Plite decorations>, while docs/vision/plite.md and the source reject generic annotation providers and use EditorRoot.

alternatives: Keeping the adopted architecture and node-key kernel is selected. The frozen benchmark kept the baseline, and every public cut has landed.

Inlining the annotation store into Plate Comments is rejected. Exact-view resolution and changed-node routing are neutral Plite jobs with raw Plite consumers (the comment-mode and persistent-anchor examples).

Replacing anchors and the index with CodeMirror RangeSet or Monaco-style decorations is rejected. Flat mapped ranges do not own roots, tree identity, authored projection or retained lifetime, and the benchmark gave no win to collection mapping.
Persisting comment attachment IDs as document marks is rejected for Comments. Target identity would enter document history and serialization while thread data has an external lifecycle.
Sharing one resolved store across mounted views is rejected, because accepted and proposed views can resolve the same retained target differently.
Replacing INVALID_ANNOTATION_RANGE_ERROR message matching with a non-throwing projection read is a local cleanup, not an architecture change, and it does not move any owner.
proofLimits: Source review only; no tests, browser or benchmark rerun. The adoption benchmark is a local frozen-gate result, not a claim against every external index; Firefox, WebKit, devices and replicated terminal absence are unexercised. The store still classifies stale ranges by matching projectRange error messages, which is a fragility no test was checked for. docs/vision/plite.md has another session's uncommitted additions; the cited lines are identical at HEAD. The root VISION.md annotation sentence is a doctrine repair owed by whoever owns VISION, not part of this verdict.
